sample_unit: admissions (MIMIC-IV) for GAVS; 21 clinical test cases for GARAG

links.outcome: Correctness of references, no duplication, formatting, and clinical appropriateness of guideline-grounded management plans
links.effect: 62 of 63 outputs (98.4%) met all criteria; the only exception was a minor ordering inconsistency in one repetition of case 14.
links.quote: Across the 63 outputs, 62 (98.4%) satisfied all evaluation criteria, with the only exception being a minor ordering inconsistency in one repetition of case 14.

links.outcome: ICD-10 subcategory recall for vector-search-constrained coding versus unconstrained direct LLM
links.effect: Subcategory recall was 20.63% (18.62% weighted) for GAVS versus 17.95% (15.86% weighted) for the vanilla LLM, P<.001; category-level recall was equal (32.60% vs 32.58%, P=.99).
links.quote: At the subcategory level, the vanilla LLM achieved 17.95% average recall (15.86% weighted), while GAVS achieved 20.63% (18.62% weighted), a statistically significant improvement (P<.001).

unlisted_practices: Generation-assisted vector search that maps LLM-generated diagnostic entities to standardized ICD-10 codes
Diagnosis-specific guideline retrieval that preserves fine-grained clinical detail (GARAG)

screen.reason: Evaluates generation-assisted retrieval-augmented generation (GARAG) and generation-assisted vector search (GAVS) against standard baseline prompts to improve grounding, accuracy, and safety in treatment planning and medical coding.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation and vector search grounding
